issues.display_title: Issue #90: Restructure the app's internal editing-tools data store for maintainability
issues.main_description_html:
Third step in the ongoing front-end cleanup effort (builds on G0 code quality setup and G1 data-handling upgrade).

Goals:

  • Eliminate the repeated outputDirectory<Tool> / logProcess<Tool> / <tool>CreateNewFile naming families (15 near-identical fields differing only by tool-name suffix).
  • Make each Edit tool's state independently readable/maintainable — isolated from the other 15 tools instead of tangled in one shared object.
  • Zero UX/behavior change — pure internal restructuring.

What changed:

  • src/renderer/features/edit/editSlice.ts — the old single file (735 lines, 91 reducers) holding state for all 16 Edit tools combined. Deleted — fully emptied after migration.
  • Added one self-contained file per tool: src/renderer/features/edit/<tool>/<tool>Slice.ts (crop, enfuse, imageResize, minifyJpg, scaleUpImage, autoLevel, equirectangularToCube, cubeToEquirectangular, imageStraightener, nadirBuilder, logoPatching, nadirPatching, stitching, roomStaging, virtualStaging2D) + a shared editShared/editSharedSlice.ts for cross-tool fields.
  • src/renderer/features/edit/editReducer.ts — now a plain Redux Toolkit combineReducers composing all 15 tool slices (previously a hand-written transitional reducer needed during the migration).
  • src/types/edit.ts — one typed state shape per tool (e.g. CropEditState, StitchingEditState) replacing the single flat EditState.
  • ~40 component/hook files across src/renderer/components/features/Edit/** updated to read/dispatch from each tool's own slice instead of the shared file.

What changed for users: Nothing — entirely behind-the-scenes. No visual or functional changes.

Why it matters: Each editing tool can now be understood, tested, and modified in isolation. Removes the naming-collision risk that made past cross-tool bugs easier to introduce.

Part of the larger front-end refactor initiative. Branch: feat/renderer-refactor-g3.

issues.display_title: Issue #55: "Don't ask again" checkbox to delete confirmation popup
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Add a "Don't ask again" checkbox inside the delete confirmation popup in the File Explorer, so users can suppress the delete warning directly from the popup without opening Preferences.

Today, the delete confirmation dialog only offers Remove / Cancel. The only way to turn the warning off is through Preferences → File Explorer → Confirm before deleting files/folders. Adding an inline checkbox makes this a one-click action at the moment of deleting.

Current behavior

  • Deleting a file/folder shows a confirmation popup with only Remove / Cancel buttons.
  • No option to suppress future warnings from the popup itself.
  • The renderer already listens for a disable-remove-warning event (IpcHandler.tsx) that sets localStorage.disableRemoveWarning = 'true', but nothing currently emits it.

Backend: src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs → confirm_remove()

app.dialog()
    .message(message)
    .title("Confirm")
    .buttons(MessageDialogButtons::OkCancelCustom("Remove".into(), "Cancel".into()))
    .blocking_show()

Note: the native Tauri plugin-dialog message dialog does not support a checkbox, so a custom modal is needed.

Proposed feature

Replace the native delete confirmation with a custom React modal (HeroUI) that includes a "Don't ask again" checkbox.

  • Popup shows: message + Remove / Cancel buttons + a "Don't ask again" checkbox (unchecked by default).
  • If the user checks it and confirms, suppress the warning for future deletes and persist it.
  • Keep this in sync with the existing Preferences → Confirm before deleting files/folders toggle (both write the same setting / flag).

Affected areas:

  • src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs (confirm_remove, delete_sources, remove_images, delete_folder) — move the confirm decision to the renderer, backend just trashes.
  • src/renderer/components/features/FileManager/ — delete flow + confirm modal.
  • src/renderer/components/core/IpcHandler.tsx — disable-remove-warning handling.
  • Preferences: confirmBeforeDeleting setting / localStorage.disableRemoveWarning.

Acceptance criteria

  • Delete confirmation popup shows a "Don't ask again" checkbox (unchecked by default).
  • Checking it + confirming suppresses future delete warnings, persisted across sessions.
  • Behavior stays in sync with the Preferences "Confirm before deleting files/folders" toggle.
  • i18n string added/reused (t_disable_remove_warning).
  • Deleting still routes to the OS recycle bin as before.

issues.display_title: Issue #62: Fix Issue Plain Click Does Not Deselect Previously Selected Image (Sticky Selection)
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback

Problem

In the file grid, a plain click (no modifier) on a second image does not clear the previous selection — the first image stays selected. Expected behavior is that a plain click selects only the clicked item and deselects everything else.

Expected selection behavior (standard file-manager semantics)

  • Plain click → select only that item; deselect all others (single selection).
  • Ctrl/Cmd + click → toggle that item's selection (add/remove) without clearing others.
  • Shift + click → select the contiguous range from the last-selected item to the clicked item.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. A plain click on an image selects only that image and clears any previous selection.
  2. Ctrl/Cmd + click adds/removes an image from the current multi-selection.
  3. Shift + click selects a contiguous range.
  4. Selection state stays consistent and predictable across clicks (no stuck/"sticky" selections).

Implement the new Edit → Scale Up Image feature.

UI design / source of truth: GoThruMedia/react-360-viewer#1422

Overview

Scale Up Image lets users enlarge photos using a local AI upscaler that runs entirely offline on the user's GPU — no cloud service, no account, no API key. It uses the bundled upscayl-bin binary (Real-ESRGAN model) to add real detail when enlarging, rather than a simple resize/interpolation.

The queue is backend-owned (Rust), so upscaling continues running in the background even if the user navigates away to another Edit tool — the queue and progress are restored automatically when the user comes back.

Feature set (as implemented)

Queue & workflow

  • Add selected images from the file browser to a queue (supports JPG, PNG, WebP).
  • Per-file table shows File Name, File Size, Resolution (current → output, computed live from the chosen scale), Status, and per-row Actions.
  • Output: toggle between overwriting the original file or saving to a new file in a chosen output folder (Browse).
  • Queue header shows live counts: Total / Queued / Success / Failed / Canceled.

Scale & performance

  • Scale multiplier: 2x–6x. 2x–4x use the AI model at its native resolution; 5x/6x apply a standard resize on top of the 4x AI result (a UI hint explains this so results aren't a surprise).
  • Performance mode, selectable per run:
    • Fastest — uses the full GPU (larger tiles, more parallel threads). Finishes sooner, but other apps may feel slower while it runs.
    • Balanced (default) — smaller tiles, single thread, below-normal process priority, so the rest of the PC stays responsive during a long queue.
  • Safety ceiling: any output image over 16384px on a side is automatically skipped with a clear error, instead of risking a GPU crash or an unreasonably large file. The Resolution column shows an inline warning (⚠️ amber for "large/slow", 🔴 red for "exceeds limit") before the user even starts the queue.

Per-item controls

  • Stop — cancel a single in-progress item; its partial output is cleaned up automatically.
  • Stop All — cancel the entire running queue at once.
  • Retry — re-queue and re-run a Failed, Canceled, or even a already-Success item.
  • View — open a completed result directly in the app's image preview.
  • Compare — for results saved as a new file, open a before/after slider (drag divider) comparing the original against the upscaled output side by side. (Not available in overwrite mode, since the original no longer exists separately.)
  • Live progress bar per item while processing (percentage parsed from the upscaler in real time).

Error handling & feedback

  • A failed-items summary modal lists every file that failed and why, after a queue run finishes with errors.
  • Built-in FAQ panel covers supported formats, offline behavior, performance modes, and common failure causes (oversized output, unsupported/missing GPU driver).

Scope note

The original spec (below) was written before implementation and described a cloud-based multiplier flow modeled on Batch Image Resize. During implementation this was replaced with a fully local/offline upscaler (no Google/cloud dependency), plus additional UX (Stop/Stop All/Retry/Compare, background queue, size guardrails) added based on follow-up product decisions. The acceptance criteria below reflect the current, shipped scope.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Users can queue images (JPG/PNG/WebP) and upscale them locally by a 2x–6x multiplier, choosing Fastest or Balanced performance.
  2. Processing runs in the background via a Rust-owned queue and survives navigating away from the Edit → Scale Up Image panel.
  3. Users can Stop/Stop All/Retry individual or all queue items, and View or Compare (before/after) a completed result.
  4. Output can either overwrite the original file or be saved as a new file in a chosen folder.
  5. Oversized targets (>16384px) are rejected safely with a clear message instead of crashing or hanging.
